title: Light-Driven Physiological Adjustments Enhance Growth Performance and Photosynthetic Efficiency in Carapa guianensis Seedlings
content: Identifying suitable environmental conditions for the early development and deciding how much to shade andiroba (Carapa guianensis Aubl.) seedlings in nurseries still lacks a technical basis. This study evaluated the growth and physiological responses of seedlings grown under 0, 30, 50, and 70% shading for 300 days, with six plants per treatment, combining chlorophyll content, chlorophyll a fluorescence, gas exchange, and growth analysis. Under full sun, the Fv/Fm ratio fell from 0.79 to 0.70 from 90 days onward, signaling photoinhibition, whereas under 70% shading values remained stable and total chlorophyll content reached five times the full-sun level by the end. Photosynthesis, stomatal conductance, and transpiration were highest under 30 and 50% shading, where carbon-use efficiency was also greatest; at 90 days, intrinsic water-use efficiency was up to 33% higher than in full sun, although all treatments declined after 180 days. The higher carbon-use efficiency under moderate shading was accompanied by greater relative growth rates, and the leaf area ratio of shaded plants was about 60% higher than in full sun. Moderate shading (30–50%) is recommended for nursery production, whereas full sun is not indicated for the early phase, as it induces pho-toinhibition and limits growth.
